Contributing ​

Thanks for helping. Marg is a design pattern as much as code; contributions that keep the pattern honest are the most valuable ones.

Before you start ​

  • Read docs/PATTERN.md and docs/PLAYBOOK.md.
  • npm install && cp .env.example .env && npm run gateway — the playground must run for you with no key (LLM_CHAIN=mock).

The gate for every change ​

bash
npm run lint                     # ESLint, correctness rules only
npm run typecheck
npm test                         # unit tests (core, verdict, metering, the widget under a fake DOM)
npm run check:otel               # the OpenTelemetry seam
npm run check:scaffold           # the templates still produce a domain that compiles and passes its suite
npm run check:e2e                # the real write path (writes ON against the example's file backend)
npm run check:pack               # every package builds and packs clean (touch a package.json or a build config)
npm run check:create             # a create-marg-app project from local tarballs installs, boots and passes its suite
npm run gateway:evals &          # writes off, :8788
npm run evals                    # the example suite must stay green

A change to a reader, a guard or a step also runs a mutation pass (break the rule in a scratch copy; the suite must go red) and adds the scenario that would have caught the bug.

Conventions ​

  • File headers: what this is, what comes in and out, who talks to it. Guard code cites the incident it stops (with a date) — in the shipped code those are real incidents.
  • Commits: Topic: imperative summary (#tag); one branch per change; a PR describes the gate it ran and classifies every red (check brittleness / flake / pre-existing / regression).
  • Observability is a definition of done: a new request-side code path ships with a span, a logged failure with the trace id, a counter or behaviour event, and check:otel green.
  • No product in the runtime: brand, vocabulary and backend specifics live in domains, shared skills and environment — never in packages/core or packages/gateway.
  • Privacy: counts and enums in telemetry labels, never a user's text; no PII in ledgers; redaction for anything that looks like a token.
  • Never weaken the write gate, the owner checks, the fail-closed identity verification or the link scheme allowlist. A PR that does is closed with a pointer here.

Adding a backend or a provider ​

Model endpoints: a preset in packages/core/src/llm.ts (base URL, auth style, defaults) and a price-table entry. Decision backends: implement DecisionBackend in packages/verdict. Speech-to-text: a provider branch in packages/gateway/src/transcribe.ts.

Pull requests ​

Open one from a branch (never push to main; it is protected). The template asks for the gate output and a classification of every red; CI runs the gate on Node 22 and 24, the packages job, CodeQL and the security checks, and a maintainer review is required. RELEASING.md describes how a merged change reaches npm.

Reporting a vulnerability ​

See SECURITY.md. Please do not open a public issue for a security problem.
